description:
## The current shape

`lib/enum.fz` has three regions, in this order: a public block, a wall of that block's private helpers, and a second public block with its helpers interleaved. `map/2`'s helper sits 240 lines from `map/2`; `frequencies/1`'s sits directly beneath it. Two conventions in one file, from two rounds of work.

## Elixir's shape

`lib/elixir/lib/enum.ex` uses two placements, and the choice between them is by role:

- A helper used by exactly one function and meaningless outside it sits immediately after that function. `flat_reverse/2` is at line 1282, right below `flat_map/2`, under a one-line comment saying why the first clause exists.
- The list fast paths live in one region near the end, alphabetical, each under a banner naming the function it serves -- `## any?/1`, `## concat`, `## count_until`, `## dedup`, `## drop`, `## filter`, `## find`.

The public API between the callback preamble and that region is alphabetical.

## What to do

One public run, alphabetical. One helper region at the end, banner-sectioned by the function served. Single-use detail helpers stay adjacent to their function. Add the `@moduledoc` the file has never had.

This is a move, not a rewrite: every clause keeps its body. Prove it by diffing the sorted inventory of function names and arities before and after -- they must be identical.

## Acceptance

- The inventory before and after is identical.
- No public function is separated from its helpers by another public function's helpers.
- Gate green; diagnostics goldens re-blessed for line drift only, confirmed by digits-stripped equality.
title: Enum: lay the module out the way Elixir lays out its own
